title: Odyssey launches world model to control robots, humanoids, vehicles and drones
source_used: Robotics & Automation News (fulltext, carries Odyssey's announcement)
key_facts: Odyssey, an AI research company, announced Odyssey-3, its most powerful 'world model'.
A world model learns from many examples of how the world changes so it can predict what happens next.
Odyssey says the model has shown it can control robots and humanoids, drive vehicles, pilot drones, generate training environments and play video games.
Flexion, which the announcement describes as a leader in humanoid autonomy, has already adopted it.
CEO Oliver Cameron calls it a big step toward a single intelligence that can operate in the world.
No test results or performance figures are given.
quote_evidence: Odyssey, an AI research company pioneering foundation world models, has announced Odyssey-3, its most powerful world model to date.
The model has shown the ability to control robots and humanoids, drive vehicles, pilot drones, generate environments for training AI agents, and play video games.
World models learn from vast examples of the world evolving to predict and simulate what happens next, including how actions affect outcomes.
why_it_matters_hint: One model that can steer many kinds of machines would make robots cheaper to teach, if the claim holds.
notes: Reads as a company announcement; no independent review. The same news is also in the pool as C01-04 (The Next Web).
